newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says reviews BT/NS Dutch telecoms alliance.
newsitem.headline: EU says reviews BT/NS Dutch telecoms alliance.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was starting a routine probe into a joint venture between British Telecommunications Plc and Dutch state-owned rail firm Nederlandse Spoorwegen (NS) to build and operate a fixed-line public telephone network in the Netherlands.
It said that at first sight the deal fell under the European Union's merger rules which ban creation or strengthening of dominant positions.
BT and NS announced earlier this month they were jointly bidding for one of the two licences the Dutch government has decided to grant in the field of telecommunications infrastructure.
The venture, formerly baptised Telecom 2, is called Telfort.
Under EU rules, telecoms markets must be fully open to competition by January 1, 1998. Dutch firm Koninklijke PTT Nederland currently has the monopoly of the country's fixed-phone network.
The other bidders for the two licences are Global One, an alliance between Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom, and a consortium of Dutch energy firms called Enertel.
The Commission has a month to clear the Telfort joint venture or start a full investigation.
